description: Conformance corpus for the default @Name:<> at-cue dialect preset (#368). Each case is a single already-trimmed source line classified in isolation (no chain context) unless `chain_after` is given, in which case `line` is classified as the line immediately following a line whose dialect kind is `chain_after`. `expect: null` means the line must NOT classify as any dialect kind (a negative fixture). This corpus is interpreter-agnostic: both the Rust classifier (`brink-ir::dialect`) and a future TS interpreter must produce identical results for every case.

cases.description: A simple character cue classifies with the name as content.
An empty-name cue template still classifies (zero-width content).
A speaker name may contain spaces.
A speaker name may contain digits and punctuation other than ':'.
A parenthetical classifies with the parens included in content.
Parenthetical content may contain punctuation other than ')'.
Narrative immediately after a cue becomes dialogue, carrying the speaker.
Narrative immediately after a parenthetical also chains to dialogue.
A dialogue run continues chaining across multiple narrative lines.
Plain narrative with no preceding cue stays narrative (no dialect match).
'@channel: hello' prose must NOT classify as a character cue — no ':<>' terminator, and the ':' is followed by prose, not the glue.
An '@' that doesn't anchor the line start is not a cue.
'@Alice:' without the '<>' glue is not a complete cue match.
'(aside) unterminated' prose must NOT classify as a parenthetical — no '<>' terminator.
'(warmly)' without the '<>' glue is not a complete parenthetical match.
A cue whose 'name' region itself contains a colon fails to match at the first colon (content_group is `[^:]*`, greedy up to the first ':') — this line does not end in ':<>' as a whole, so no match.
